🧪 Trials — test a suspect food properly
A controlled test the app scores for you. Avoid one food for a few days while it watches your check-in scores against your recent baseline, then optionally reintroduce it to confirm. Because you log everything, it can verify you actually stuck to the trial.
📓 What I've learned
Your accumulated conclusions in one place, fusing three sources: your own labels (set in 📋 Summary), the ⚖️ Verdicts analysis, and your 🧪 Trial results. Trial-proven findings rank first. Where a food's signals disagree, it's flagged for you to settle — nothing is silently overridden.

⚖️ Verdicts — one combined judgement per food
ℹ️ How to read this tab

What this is: one plain verdict per food, so you don't have to cross-read the other analysis tabs. It answers a single question — does this food react more, less, or about the same as your typical food?

Why “compared to your typical food”: your body reacts to most things — your baseline ✕ rate is high (shown at the top of the list). So “totally safe” isn't realistic here; instead every food is graded against your own average. A food that reacts less than usual is a genuine win.

The four groups:

  • 🔺 Suspect — reacts MORE than your average. Your prime candidates to cut or test.
  • 🟡 Typical — behaves like your average food. Neutral.
  • 🟢 Easier on you — reacts LESS than your average. Your safer choices — lean on these during flares.
  • ❔ Unclear — you haven't marked enough reaction windows for this food yet.

The small tags: strong / some / weak evidence = how many reaction windows back the verdict (more windows = more trustworthy). 📌 staple = you eat it almost daily, so no day-comparison can isolate it — use 🧪 Test to know for sure.

The evidence line: the colored chip is the reaction window (hours after eating), the big percentage is this food's ✕ rate there, and the grey one is your baseline. The two mini bars draw the same comparison — top bar = this food, bottom bar = your baseline.

How to act: tap 🧪 Test on any Suspect to run a controlled trial that actually proves whether it's the culprit.

Insights

Food Summary

Filter the summary by date range, hide low-data foods, and use confidence + safe/risky cards to focus on stronger patterns first. Dominant window color still shows the main outcome: green = mostly positive, red = mostly negative.

Face Map

Tap a region on the face to link foods to skin reactions at that spot. Search a food above the face to light up every region it has been marked on. Rotate between the front, left and right views to cover the whole face.

Food Profile

Everything the app knows about one food, in one place — pulled from the same engines as Verdicts, Insights, the Face Map and Trials, so the numbers always agree.

⏱️ Reaction Timeline (Day 0 to Day +5)
• How your symptoms in the days after a food compare to your usual level for that symptom.
• A pattern spotter, not a verdict: it surfaces foods worth a closer look. To actually confirm a trigger, tap 🧪 Test to run a Trial.
• Enhanced shows each day vs your baseline (so a number means something). Legacy is the old absolute-score view.
Food / Item Day 0 Day +1 Day +2 Day +3 Day +4 Day +5
Statistical Analysis:
• Compares check-ins on days exactly N days after you ate a food vs. all other days. (The Correlations tab instead uses a cumulative "day 0 to +N" window.)
• For 1–5 scores the % is a scale-shift, not a probability; for meal tags it is a probability change.
• Relative mode needs at least 3 exposed and 3 control days; foods that can't meet that are counted in the note below, not silently dropped.
• The Timeline tab shows the day-by-day shape of the days after a food instead.
